review:
# Independent generation escrow review

Reviewed immutable manifest 1869acd268bca8c69bd62d8edc7a5616c7cbc7d102af8f5da2c8dd9f4a69b5fd.
All copied payload hashes and immutable ad67 provider were checked before
execution; INPUTS.json records them. No Root/author source or frozen package
was changed and no whole-Core build was run.

No concrete publication-before-sync, foreign-permit, copy-identity, lock,
cursor or ordinary-write regression was found in the reviewed scope.

I independently compiled the exact metadata include closure with Rust1.90 and
the immutable actual ad67 public provider. All ten escrow tests passed
(escrow-tests.log). Two additional isolated reviewer controls passed
(reviewer-tests.log): the independently compiled old provider actually opened,
read, wrote and pruned the new guarded catalog after publication; and the
same-handle copy restored a deliberately nondefault file cursor after digest,
successful copy and create-new failure, retaining the prefix and allowing
the next real append. Those reviewer controls modify only the review copy's
test-module includes, not the reviewed production code.

The copied journal, GENINFO and RECORD are synced before rename. The explicit
directory-sync profile syncs pending directories and the publication root;
the retry path also syncs the root before accepting an already present copy.
An unpublished pending directory yields no permit. The source/current prefix
is rechecked before publication and the final copy is reopened/fingerprinted
under its actual exclusive Journal lock before the private permit returns.

The live permit binds the actual owner token and exact current verified
prefix. A cold descriptor/snapshot has no constructor for that permit.
Guarded compaction and cross-publication append retain the locked copied-file
owner throughout the original publication/prune operation. Original/copy
locations remain separate: the record binds original identity/publication,
requested full-KV points, canonical copied root, original manifest and exact
raw log fingerprint. Cold reads map original logical to copied physical
sequence explicitly and return a distinct readonly snapshot.

The ten tests exercise actual removal of the original old generation, later
old-reader pruning, source-owner close, corrupt/missing log/manifest/record,
foreign and stale permits, wrong original/copy identity, pending publication
failure, guarded automatic-compaction append, no-copy ordinary append and a
complete 1100-row stream. Partial/forged row expectations refuse. The new
public sidecars are include-only pure transforms; existing original commit,
prepare-put, journal-format and prune bodies remain unchanged. The independent
old-provider read/write control additionally verifies that compatibility with
an already compiled older interpreter, rather than self-comparing two calls
to the proposed module.

All executed durability cases used the explicit Windows FileSyncOnly profile.
They establish file sync/process-owner-close behavior, not directory durability
or power-loss survival. The FileAndDirectorySync branch was inspected and is
explicitly unavailable on this host; it was not executed. Active-service/WAL
callers are still required to select the guarded APIs at their actual
cross-publication boundary. This metadata escrow does not by itself establish
financial cold replay or authenticated provenance. No additional production
change is requested from this review.
